name: Ascent to yoga in Bhagavad Gītā 6 (ārurukṣu → yogārūḍha → the highest peace)

stages.name: ārurukṣu
stages.gloss: one wishing to ascend to yoga
stages.description: For the sage wishing to ascend to yoga, action (karma) is said to be the means (6.3); cf. yogins act, abandoning attachment, for self-purification (5.11).

stages.name: yogārūḍha
stages.gloss: one who has ascended to yoga
stages.description: For the same sage once ascended, calm (śama) is said to be the means (6.3); he is called ascended when he is attached neither to sense-objects nor to actions and has renounced all intentions (6.4).

stages.name: nirvāṇa-paramā śānti / parā gati
stages.gloss: peace culminating in nirvāṇa; the highest course
stages.description: The constantly yoked yogin with controlled mind attains peace culminating in nirvāṇa, abiding in the Lord (6.15); the striving yogin, cleansed and perfected through many births, reaches the highest course (6.45).

notes: Only stages 1–2 are given as an explicit sequence by the text (6.3); stage 3 is the chapter's own statement of the result. The intermediate states the chapter describes (6.18–23, 6.27–32) are recorded as phenomenology. Band assignments are interpretive.
